name: PullbackLegCounter
quote: In a sideways or downward move in a bull trend or a trading range, the first bar whose high is above the high of the prior bar is a high 1, and this ends the first leg... If the market does not turn into a bull swing and instead continues sideways or down, label the next occurrence... as a high 2.
description: Shared primitive: while a pullback (sideways/down move in a bull trend) is in progress, count each bar whose high exceeds the prior bar's high as ending one leg of the pullback; the running count is the current leg number (high-1, high-2, ...). Resets when the pullback ends (a swing back to a new trend extreme) or the trend context changes. Mirror: low-N counts bars whose low is below the prior bar's low during a bear-trend/range pullback.
pseudocode: legCount = 0; for each bar since pullback start: if high[bar] > high[bar+1]: legCount += 1 (only the first such bar per leg counts, i.e. the counter does not increment again until the pullback resumes making lower highs)

complexity.reason: a persistent cross-bar counter with reset logic tied to identifying when a pullback starts and ends

notes: This is the core of Brooks's H1/H2/H3/H4 and L1/L2/L3/L4 bar-counting system, arguably the single most load-bearing primitive in the whole trilogy.

name: PullbackSizeSinceTrendStart
quote: Look at the size of the pullbacks since the trend began. For example, in a small pullback bull trend, if the largest pullback in the past couple of hours has been only eight ticks, buy with a limit order at five to seven ticks below the high of the day.
